title: Regroup the CLI around status, story and run, modelled on gh

steps.reason: Spec written: gh-style CLI tree (status / story / run / setup / background / agent), B1–B71 with examples, out of scope, no open questions. Key decisions: noun stays story until #74; status = inbox+cockpit with one-time notice; no aliases; run cancel parks; story close/reopen; story create stops at intake; config set/unset --user|--repo (#64 to build on it).

events.summary: claude turn_start Use the norn skill, then run `norn brief`.

claude turn_end I've read the story, the current `norn help`, PRD §15 and the rules it touches (MO5, S7, GR7, BS9, K2a, P8), plus the two related issues, #74 (renaming the noun "story") and #64 (minimal config). I'll interview you one question at a time, in this order: problem, solution, behaviour, scope. **Q1 (Problem): who is this for, and when does it bite?** From the issue and the code, I'd frame it like this: > A person running norn: one developer, or a teammate taking a story over. They hit it each time they have to act: answer a question, approve a gate, unblock a stuck unit, start a step. Today they must pick from 29 flat commands across five overlapping views. Several names mislead (`drop` cancels the story; `update` sounds like a self-update; `release` sounds like shipping a version; `open` starts a step). One verb does three jobs (`unstick`). The flags change what a command does (`approve --reject`, `orient --open`). The cost: they look things up in `norn help` or the inbox's printed command instead of guessing, and they can pick the wrong one, for example `drop` when they only wanted to stop an agent. Four things have no command at all: creating a story, stopping a running agent, undoing a drop, and setting a config value. Does that match? Two parts I'd like you to sharpen: - **Who does it hurt most?** You, day to day? A newcomer to norn? An agent that reads the printed commands? - **Has a wrong command actually happened?** For example, a `drop` that was meant as a "stop". If so, it should lead the Problem.
claude turn_start it hurst everyone by bringing chaos, so it hard to orient for norn users, agent etc. In this approach long run maintaance is hard

claude turn_end Got it: the problem is that the surface is chaotic for everyone (people, newcomers and agents reading printed commands), and that chaos makes norn hard to maintain over time. I'll write it that way. **Q2 (Solution): which noun goes in the middle of the tree?** The tree is `norn status` / `norn <noun> <verb>` / `norn run <verb>`. The middle noun is the word people will type most, and #74 (rename "story") is still open, with **change** as its current favourite. The options: - **A. Use `story` now, and rename the command along with #74 later.** This story doesn't wait on #74, but if #74 picks "change", the command gets renamed twice: `status`→`story list`→`change list`, with a second set of aliases. - **B. Settle #74 first, inside this refine.** You decide the noun now, and the spec uses it. #74 then covers the persisted names (`story.md`, branches, schema) and this story covers only the CLI noun. - **C. Block this story until #74 lands.** **Recommended: B.** The CLI noun is what people type and what every printed command shows, so it's the expensive part to change twice. Settling it here doesn't mean renaming files: the persisted rename can stay in #74. If B, which noun: **story** (keep it, and accept issue numbers as keys) or **change**?
claude turn_end Claude is waiting for your input

claude turn_end A: the noun is `story` for now. Renaming it is #74's job, and that story would carry its own aliases. **Q3 (Solution): does `norn status` take the "what needs you" meaning?** Today `norn status` lists stories, slices, runs and claims. The proposal makes it the inbox, which replaces `inbox` and `cockpit`, and moves today's listing to `story list`. So anyone who types `status` out of habit gets a different screen. - **A. Take the name, as gh does (`gh status` = what needs you).** For one minor release, `status` prints a one-time notice: "`status` now shows what needs you; the story listing moved to `norn story list`." The notice goes to stderr and appears once per checkout. - **B. Keep `inbox` as the overview** and retire `status` (or alias it to `story list`). **Recommended: A.** "Status" is the word people reach for first, and gh users already expect it to mean this. One sub-question if A: should the notice show **once per checkout** (recorded locally) or **every time, for one minor release**? I'd go with once per checkout.
claude turn_start A. btw how we gonna open cockpit in new approach

claude turn_end A: `status` takes the new meaning. For the notice I'll go with "once per checkout", since you didn't object. **How the cockpit opens in the new layout.** Today `norn cockpit` has three modes, and each one maps across: | Today | New | What you see | |---|---|---| | `norn cockpit` | `norn status --watch` | The same full-screen live cockpit in your terminal: what needs you, every story, a preview of the selected row, keys for the actions. It stays open until q or Esc. | | `norn cockpit --open` | `norn status --watch --pane` | Splits a Herdr pane below yours and runs the cockpit there. The Herdr plugin's `cockpit.sh` calls this, so you'd normally reach it through the plugin's key binding, not by typing it. | | `norn cockpit --next` | `norn run attach` (no argument, outside a unit) | Jumps to the agent pane of the oldest "Your turn" item. | | `norn cockpit --json` | `norn status --json` | Prints the model once. | Plain `norn status` (no `--watch`) prints the inbox once, the way `norn inbox` does today. **Q4: should `--pane` be in help, or hidden?** - **A. Hidden.** It shows only in `help --all`, and the Herdr plugin is the way in. - **B. Public**, listed under `status` in normal help, so someone without the plugin's key binding can split a pane by hand. **Recommended: B.** It costs one line of help, and a person inside Herdr has no other way to discover it. The issue said hidden, so this would change it; your call.
claude turn_end Claude is waiting for your input

claude turn_end B: `--pane` is public. **Q5: how does a person move a unit to another step?** Today there are two ways: `unstick --to <step>` (same workflow, while the unit is stuck) and `workflow <unit> <name> --to <step>` (switch the workflow and pick a step; S7). The proposal splits it like this: - `norn run rerun --step <step>` moves within the same workflow (replaces `unstick --to`). - `norn story edit --workflow <name> --at <step>` switches the workflow (replaces `workflow --to`). Two questions in one, since they hang together: 1. **Keep both, as above?** Alternative: one place only, `story edit --at <step>` (with or without `--workflow`), with `run rerun` limited to re-running the current step. 2. **When does `rerun --step` apply?** Today `unstick` works only on a stuck or parked unit. Should `rerun --step` also work on a unit that is **running** (it would cancel the run first) or **waiting at a gate**? **Recommended:** keep both, since they're different actions: rerun means "this step again or a nearby one", edit means "change the plan". `rerun` applies to stuck, parked and gate-waiting units. A running unit is refused with "`norn run cancel` first", so stopping an agent is always explicit.

claude turn_end I read "both" as keeping both commands: `run rerun --step` moves within the workflow, and `story edit --workflow --at` switches workflow. Please confirm the second part too: `rerun` works on stuck, parked and gate-waiting units, and a running unit is refused with "`norn run cancel` first". Correct me if I'm wrong. **Q6: what does `norn run cancel` do?** It's new: today the only way to stop an agent is `drop`, which cancels the whole story. My proposal: - It stops the running agent session for a unit (kills the session, closes or leaves the Herdr pane) and writes a receipt. - The unit then **parks** with reason `cancelled by person`. It shows under Unblock in `norn status`, and the next tick does not start it again. - From there: `norn run rerun` resumes the same step in a fresh session, `rerun --step` moves it, and `story close` ends the story. - The story, branch, worktree, claim and the work so far stay untouched (commits stay; uncommitted changes stay in the worktree). - Only the checkout that holds the claim can cancel. Others are refused with "`norn story checkout` first", the same as other session effects. - A unit with no running session is refused with `nothing_to_cancel`. The open choice is the **Herdr pane: close it, or leave it open** so you can read what the agent was doing? **Recommended: leave it open.** `tidy` already cleans panes of finished runs. Agree, or change any part?

claude turn_end Agreed. `run cancel` parks the unit and leaves the pane open. **Q7: `story close` and `story reopen`.** `story close` replaces `drop` and keeps its effects: it pushes the branches, then removes the worktrees, local branches and the claim. The record stays (spec, runs, receipts on the branch). It leaves the remote issue and PR alone (GR7). Here is what I'd pin down: 1. **Confirmation.** Close is the only verb that deletes local worktrees. Should it ask "Close gh-75? Worktrees for 3 units will be removed [y/N]" in a terminal, and need `--yes` under `--json` or with no TTY? **Recommended: yes.** 2. **What `reopen` restores.** **Recommended:** it re-claims the story on this checkout, re-creates the worktrees from the pushed branches, and puts every unit back where it was when closed, at the same step. A unit that was running comes back parked (`reopened`), so nothing starts by itself. A person then runs `run rerun`. 3. **When `reopen` refuses.** Recommended: when the story isn't closed (`not_closed`), when its branch is gone from the remote, or when the remote issue is closed (it says to reopen the issue first, since GR7 would park the story anyway). 4. **Close on a story another machine holds.** Recommended: refused, "`norn story checkout` first", as for `drop` today. Agree to all four, or adjust?

claude turn_end Agreed on close and reopen. **Q8: `norn story create`.** Today a story starts only as a labelled issue on the remote, which the next `sync` takes in. My proposal: - `norn story create --title "…" [--body "…" | --body-file <f>] [--workflow <name>]` creates the issue on the remote (gh or glab) with the `norn` label, plus `norn:wf:<name>` when a workflow is given, assigned to you. It then runs an intake sync right away and prints the new story key (`gh-81`). So it's the same path as a hand-made issue, with no second way in (GR1). - In a terminal with no `--title`, it prompts for the title, then opens `$EDITOR` for the body, like `gh issue create`. Under `--json` or with no TTY, a missing `--title` is refused. - An unknown `--workflow` is refused before anything is created, listing the workflows available. - If the remote is unreachable or auth fails, nothing is created locally, and the error says what to fix (`norn doctor`). - `--web` opens the remote's new-issue page instead, with the label pre-filled. The open sub-question: should `create` also **start** the story (claim it and make the worktree), or stop at intake? **Recommended: stop at intake.** Starting is a separate decision, and the story appears under "Your turn" or "Unclaimed" in `norn status` like any other. Agree?

claude turn_end Agreed. **Q9: `norn config set`, which depends on #64 (minimal config in three files).** The question is which file `set` writes to. Today there are two layers (user `~/.norn/config.yaml` and repo `.agents/norn/config.yaml`). #64 would make three files, each key legal in only one of them. - **A. Build it on today's two layers now:** `config set <key> <value> [--user|--repo]`, with the repo file as the default. Validate before writing, and on a bad value refuse and leave the file unchanged. Comments and key order in the file are kept. #64 later changes which file a key goes to. - **B. Make `config set` wait for #64.** This story ships `config list` and `config get` only, and `set` lands with #64, where each key's file is fixed so no `--user`/`--repo` flag is needed. **Recommended: B.** Under #64 the file follows from the key, so `config set mode auto` just works. Building A first means designing flags that #64 removes, and a write path that has to be redone.
claude turn_start so integrate #64 to this issue

claude turn_end Before I write that down, here's what it would mean. #64 is not a small add-on: it rewrites the config model (37 keys down to 14, three files, new error codes, derived claim timing, workflow `defaults:`, `config --migrate`), with its own 8-step plan and several breaking changes. It's about as big as this story. **Q10: how much of #64 comes in?** - **A. All of #64.** This story also delivers the three-file config model and every key change, and #64 closes as a duplicate. The spec roughly doubles, and the release carries two breaking changes (commands and config) at once. - **B. Only the `config` commands, on #64's model.** This story ships `config list`, `config get`, `config set <key> <value>` and `config unset`, written for #64's three files (the file follows from the key; a key in the wrong file is refused). #64 still delivers the model itself, and the `config set` slice waits for it. - **C. Fold #64's command-facing parts in, keep the model separate.** This story takes the `config` verbs plus `config --migrate` (as `config migrate`) and the new config error codes in help and output. The model stays in #64. **Recommended: B.** It gives the command surface its final shape now, keeps each release to one breaking change, and #64 stays reviewable on its own. Which do you mean?
claude turn_start Let's go with A we gonna rewrite #64 to this

claude turn_end A: `config set` ships here on today's two layers, and #64 gets rewritten to build on it. I'll note that under Related. **Q10: details of `config set`.** 1. **Default file when neither `--user` nor `--repo` is given.** I said repo, but the repo file is committed, so a personal setting (`default_mode auto`) would land in the team's file. Options: **default to user**; or **refuse without a flag**; or default to repo. **Recommended: refuse without a flag** in a non-TTY or `--json` run, and prompt for the file in a terminal ("Write to user (~/.norn/config.yaml) or repo (.agents/norn/config.yaml)?"). 2. **Removing a value.** Add `config unset <key> [--user|--repo]`, or reuse the existing `null` with `config set <key> null`? **Recommended: `config unset`**, since gh has `config set` only, but unsetting by `null` is hard to guess. 3. **Nested and list keys.** Dotted paths (`limits.deadline 90m`, `agents.claude.model opus`) with YAML-parsed values. A list (`notifiers`) is set whole as YAML (`'[{adapter: os}]'`). Agree?
claude turn_end Claude is waiting for your input

claude turn_end Agreed on all three. **Q11: default target and prompts** (`story <verb> [<story|slice>]`, `run <verb> [<run|unit>]`). Here's what I'd propose: 1. **Inside a unit worktree:** the target is that worktree's unit. Story verbs from a slice worktree act on the slice (`approve`, `answer`, `checkout` are per unit). Verbs that only make sense on a story (`close`, `reopen`, `edit --workflow` before start, `handoff`, `update-branch`) act on the slice's story. 2. **Outside a unit worktree, in a terminal:** the command prompts with a pick-list of only the units the verb applies to (`story approve` lists units waiting at a gate). The list is ordered as in `norn status`. 3. **Exactly one candidate:** still prompt, with it preselected. **No candidates:** refuse with the reason ("Nothing waits at a gate") and exit `refused`. 4. **Under `--json`, with no TTY, or when run by an agent:** never prompt. A missing target is refused with a `CliError` that lists the candidate keys in `do_instead`. 5. **An explicit argument always wins over the worktree,** so `norn story approve gh-12` works from anywhere. The open choice is point 3. **Recommended: confirm even with one candidate,** because acting on the wrong unit is costly. The alternative is to act on it straight away and print what it acted on.
claude turn_end Claude is waiting for your input

claude turn_end Agreed. **Q12: aliases for the old names.** Three parts: 1. **How long.** Old names (`inbox`, `cockpit`, `orient`, `open`, `answer`, `approve`, `unstick`, `update`, `mode`, `workflow`, `take`, `release`, `drop`, `trace`, `why`, `config [<key>]`) stay as hidden aliases for **one minor release**, then go in a later release. The alternative is to keep them for good. **Recommended: one minor**, because keeping them means maintaining two surfaces, which is the problem this story fixes. 2. **The hint.** Every use prints a hint on stderr each time, for example `norn: 'drop' is now 'norn story close'`. stdout and `--json` are untouched, and the exit codes are the same. Every time, not once, so scripts' logs show it. Agree? 3. **`status <key>`.** `status` is taken by the new meaning, but `norn status gh-12` (with a story key) has no meaning in the new surface. **Recommended:** for the alias release, treat `status <key>` as `story view <key>`, with the hint. Plain `status` gets the new meaning plus the one-time notice from Q3. Agree?

claude turn_end No aliases, then. That leaves one follow-up. **Q13: what happens when someone types an old name?** For example `norn drop gh-12`, from habit, an old script, or an old README. - **A. A pointer, not an alias.** The command doesn't run. It refuses with exit `usage` and a `CliError`: `"drop" was renamed`, do_instead `norn story close gh-12` (with the arguments carried across where they map). This works for every old name, with no end date and no second code path, because it only names the new command. - **B. Plain unknown command**, like any typo, with a pointer to `norn help`. **Recommended: A.** It never acts, so it keeps nothing of the old surface alive, but it saves everyone a trip to the docs. Related points I'll assume unless you object: - The Herdr plugin scripts, README, CONTRIBUTING, skills and AGENTS.md switch to the new names in the same release. Installed hook configs keep working, since `hook` is unchanged. - The `status` one-time notice from Q3 stays. - Same release. This is a breaking change to the CLI: a minor bump before 1.0.

claude turn_end B: an old name is a plain unknown command that points to `norn help`. The other assumptions stand (docs, plugin and skills updated in the same release; the `status` notice stays; a minor bump). **Q14: how help is grouped.** `norn help` would show: ``` Core norn status What needs you, across every story (--watch, --pane, --history, --details, --notes) norn story Stories and slices: create, list, view, answer, approve, reject, update-branch, start, chat, edit, checkout, handoff, close, reopen norn run Runs of a step: list, view, attach, rerun, cancel Setup norn init · doctor · config · uninstall Background norn watch · sync · tidy Agent protocol (the only commands an agent runs) norn brief · done · ask · stuck ``` - `norn story` with no verb (or `norn help story`) lists its verbs in the four groups: general, decision, work, team. The same goes for `run`. - `help --all` adds `tick`, `hook` and `status --segment`. - The agent preamble ("Agent doing a norn step? Run only `norn brief`…") and the skills list stay. **Recommended:** as above. Agree, or would you rather `help` list every verb in full instead of `norn story`'s one-line summary?

claude turn_end **Q15: `run attach` without a target, as the Herdr plugin uses it.** The plugin's "next" key runs today's `cockpit --next --json`: with no TTY, it focuses the agent pane of the oldest "Your turn" item. Under Q11, `run attach` with no target and no TTY would refuse. So the plugin needs a non-interactive form: - **A. `norn run attach --next`:** pick the oldest "Your turn" unit with a live pane, and never prompt. If there is none, refuse with `nothing_to_attach` and give the unit's start command when it has no pane. - **B. The plugin works out the unit itself** (`status --json`, then `run attach <unit>`). That needs shell parsing in the plugin. **Recommended: A.** It keeps the plugin a one-liner and is also handy at a terminal. The rest of the mapping I'll write as below unless you object: - **`story view`** merges today's `status <key>` and `orient`: slices, PR, open notes, and what waits for you. With `--web` it opens the PR if there is one, else the issue. - **`story start [--print]`** = `open`. **`story chat`** = `orient --open`. - **`story reject`** requires `--reason`. Today it's optional on `approve --reject`, and a rejection without a reason gives the next attempt nothing to go on. - **`story edit`:** - `--auto`/`--manual` = `mode`. - `--workflow <name>` before start = `workflow`. - After start, `--workflow` needs `--at <step>`, otherwise it's refused as `workflow --to` is today (S7). - `--auto` and `--manual` together is a usage error. - **`run list`** = `trace` (same flags). **`run view`** shows one run: step, attempt, outcome, durations, receipts. `--why` = `why`, `--receipt <id>` = `why --receipt`. - **Targets of `run` verbs:** a run id or a unit key. A unit key means its latest run. - **Printed commands:** the commands norn prints (inbox items, `do_instead`, handoff, briefs, cockpit actions) all use the new names in the same release.

claude turn_end A: `run attach --next`. I'll write the rest of the mapping as listed. **Q16 (Scope): what's out of this story?** Proposed out of scope: - **User-defined aliases** (`gh alias set`): not now, per the issue. - **Renaming the noun "story"**: that's #74, which brings its own CLI rename. - **Three config files and key moves**: that's #64, rewritten to build on `config set`. - **Shell completion**: a separate story. The noun tree makes it easy later. - **Changes to the agent protocol, `hook`, receipt kinds, `state.json`, trace events, exit codes, the `CliError` shape or the `--json` shapes of moved commands**: all unchanged. - **New views or changes to inbox grouping** (O1 groups stay): `status` shows what `inbox` and `cockpit` show today. - **`--repo`/`-R` to act on another repository from anywhere**: not now. Anything to add or move in?

claude turn_end Here is the summary to confirm before I write the spec. Points 9 and 11 are my additions for a few edges. 1. **Problem:** 29 flat commands, overlapping views, misleading names, flags that change what a command does, and missing actions. It's chaotic for people and agents to find their way, and hard to maintain. 2. **Tree:** `norn status` / `norn story <verb>` / `norn run <verb>`, plus Setup (`init`, `doctor`, `config list|get|set|unset`, `uninstall`), Background (`watch`, `sync`, `tidy`) and Agent (`brief`, `done`, `ask`, `stuck`). `tick`, `hook` and `status --segment` appear only in `help --all`. The noun stays `story` until #74. 3. **`status`** is what needs you. It replaces `inbox` and `cockpit`: - `--watch` gives the live cockpit, and `--pane` opens it in a Herdr split (public). - `--history`, `--details`, `--notes` and `--json` work as today. - A one-time notice per checkout on stderr says the story listing moved to `story list`. 4. **Moving a unit to another step:** - `run rerun [--step] [--reset] [--reason]` works on stuck, parked and gate-waiting units; a running unit is refused with "run cancel first". - `story edit --workflow <name> --at <step>` switches workflow; after start it needs `--at`. 5. **`run cancel`** stops the session and parks the unit (`cancelled by person`) with a receipt. Work, claim and pane stay. Only the holder may cancel. With no session it's refused (`nothing_to_cancel`). 6. **`story close`** has today's `drop` effects: - It asks for confirmation in a terminal, and needs `--yes` otherwise. - It's refused when another machine holds the story. 7. **`story reopen`:** - It re-claims the story, re-creates the worktrees, and puts each unit back at its step; a unit that was running comes back parked. - It's refused when the story isn't closed, its branch is gone, or the issue is closed. 8. **`story create`:** - It takes `--title`, `--body`/`--body-file` and `--workflow`. - In a terminal it prompts and opens `$EDITOR`. `--web` opens the remote's new-issue page. - It creates the labelled, assigned issue, takes it in, prints the key, and does not start it. - Nothing is created on a bad workflow or a remote failure. 9. **`config set|unset <key> [--user|--repo]`:** - Dotted keys and YAML values. - Without a flag it prompts for the file in a terminal, and refuses otherwise. - A bad value or unknown key is refused, and the file is unchanged. - Comments are kept. 10. **Targets:** - The default is the worktree's unit; story-only verbs go to its story. - Outside a unit worktree it prompts with only the units that apply, and confirms even with one; it refuses when there are none. - It never prompts under `--json`, with no TTY, or for an agent; then it refuses and lists the candidates. - An explicit argument wins. 11. **The rest of the mapping, per Q15:** `run attach --next` for the plugin. `story reject --reason` is required. `story view --web`. `run view` shows a run, with `--why` and `--receipt`. A unit key given to `run` verbs means its latest run. Closing a closed story is refused (`already_closed`). 12. **No aliases.** An old name is an unknown command pointing to `norn help`. Docs, plugin, skills, AGENTS.md and every printed command switch in the same release, as a minor bump. 13. **Help tiers**, as in Q14. 14. **Out of scope**, as in Q16. **Related:** #74, and #64 to be rewritten on top of `config set`. Is this what you meant? If yes, I'll write the spec.

claude turn_end I've written the spec into the body of `.agents/specs/gh-75-regroup-the-cli-around-status-story-and/story.md`; the frontmatter is unchanged. I'll report this step done once you agree it says what you meant. What's in it: - **Problem and Solution**, from the user's side, with the full map from today's commands to the new ones. - **Behaviour B1–B71**, each with an example: - help and the shape of the surface: B1–B8 - `status`: B9–B14 - `story` general: B15–B23 - `story` decision: B24–B27 - `story` work: B28–B32 - `story` team, including close and reopen: B33–B42 - `run`, including cancel: B43–B53 - targets and prompts: B54–B60 - `config` list, get, set and unset: B61–B68 - what stays unchanged: B69–B71 - **Out of scope**, as agreed in Q16, plus the "no aliases" decision. - **Open questions:** none. - **Related:** #74 (the noun) and #64 (to be rewritten on top of `config set`/`unset`). A few points come from the summary, not from separate questions, so check they read right: - **B39:** closing a story that's already closed is refused (`already_closed`). - **B68:** unsetting a key the file doesn't have changes nothing and exits 0. - **B71:** the PRD's command table (§15) and every rule that names an old command are rewritten in this story. Does the spec say what you meant?

done done at refine#1 — Spec written: gh-style CLI tree (status / story / run / setup / background / agent), B1–B71 with examples, out of scope, no open questions. Key decisions: noun stays story until #74; status = inbox+cockpit with one-time notice; no aliases; run cancel parks; story close/reopen; story create stops at intake; config set/unset --user|--repo (#64 to build on it).

claude turn_end I've reported the refine step for gh-75 as done; norn decides the next step from here. The spec is in `.agents/specs/gh-75-regroup-the-cli-around-status-story-and/story.md`. It has Behaviour items B1–B71, each with an example, an Out of scope list, and no open questions. For you to do outside this story: - **#64 needs rewriting:** this story ships `config set` and `config unset` with `--user`/`--repo` on today's two config files, and #64 should build on that. - **#74 still settles the noun:** the commands say `story` until it lands, and its rename of the commands is its own work.

steps.reason: Plan agreed with the person: seams S1 runCli harness (+ interaction fake), S2 old-name repo lint, S3 remote contract; coverage for B1–B71; 3 prefactors (noun–verb framework, one printed-commands module, take restore extracted); D1–D9 (cancel = human stuck receipt, story view = orient JSON extended, prompts only TTY+no --json+not agent). B41/B51/B70 wording amended.

units.title: Regroup the CLI around status, story and run, modelled on gh
Noun–verb command tree, with run list and run view
One module builds every command norn prints
Targets from the worktree, and terminal prompts
norn status shows what needs you; the listing moves to story list
status --watch replaces the cockpit; run attach
story view and story chat replace status <key> and orient
story answer, approve, reject and update-branch
story create, with the remote's createIssue
config list, get, set and unset
Printed commands use the new names; help shows the whole tree
Docs, skills, Herdr plugin and PRD on the new names, held by a lint
